data.title: Autos, financials power India market rally, defying broader Asia decline
data.description:
By Bharath Rajeswaran and Vivek Kumar M

Indian shares bucked a broader Asian selloff on Thursday, led by auto and financial stocks, as falling commodity prices and steady foreign buying outweighed losses in IT stocks following hawkish US Federal Reserve comments.

The Nifty 50 rose 1.14% to 25,514.30, while the Sensex gained 1.21% to 83,021.75.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) fell 1.7%, as fears over the AI trade and hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials left sentiment fragile ahead of a blockbuster market debut from Anthropic.

A reversal of foreign flows to India after about two years, when an AI-led emerging markets rally had drawn much of the foreign capital, is powering the current rally, said analysts led by Bino Pathiparampil, head of research at Elara Capital.

The Nifty and Sensex have gained 10.7% and 11.5% in November, supported by record monthly foreign inflows worth $11.28 billion on robust earnings and 21.6% fall in crude prices.

"While valuation cushion has narrowed, healthy earnings growth underpins our constructive market view," Pathiparampil said.

Fifteen of 16 major sectors advanced. The broader small-cap and mid-cap indexes added about 0.7% and 1.1%, respectively.

Auto index climbed 4.4% on easing commodity prices and strong festival sales. Maruti Suzuki India topped Nifty gainers with a 7.6% surge.

AC makers Voltas and Blue Star also gained 9% and 8.8% as copper prices fell to a near seven-month low on Wednesday.

Banks , financials , private banks (.NIFPVTBNK) and state-owned lenders gained between 1.1% and 2.3%. They have climbed between 13.6% and 18.6% so far this month.

IT index was the sole loser among major sectors on the day, dropping 1.1%, after US Federal Reserve's October meeting minutes meeting showed that policymakers saw a need to intensify efforts to curb inflation.

The likelihood of higher US rates renewed concerns about client technology spending, according to analysts. Indian IT companies derive a significant share of revenue from the United States.

Online-payment firms Paytm , One Mobikwik and Pine Labs fell 8.7%, 8.3% and 4.8%, respectively, following reports of a potential delay in the government's rollout of the merchant discount rate.

data.title: Stocks look to break losing streak ahead of blockbuster Anthropic IPO
data.description:
Key points:
  • Anthropic's blockbuster IPO pricing helps lifts Nasdaq futures Ongoing investor worries over AI trade linger
  • Hawkish Fed lifts dollar to 19-month high, nudges up bond yields

By Marc Jones and Ankur Banerjee

World stocks were in danger of setting their longest losing streak of the year on Thursday as bruised bulls pinned their hopes on Anthropic's blockbuster market debut later in the day to lift the otherwise fragile mood.

Asian markets hadn't fully read the script as Taiwan and Hong Kong both fell heavily overnight, but Europe's tech stocks quickly caught the thermal in early trading while Nasdaq futures jumped nearly 1.7% ahead of Wall Street's open.

Elsewhere, gold remained stuck near a 14-month low and benchmark government bond yields ticked up following talk of at least a further 50 basis points worth of US rate rises. But for the time being it was mostly background noise.

Claude-developer Anthropic's IPO is set to be the largest flotation of all time. Its shares were priced at a lofty $83 apiece, valuing the firm at about $1.5 trillion.

"At $83 per share, Anthropic is coming to market above its initial pricing range, but still below our $92 fair value estimate," said Malik Ahmed Khan, a senior equity analyst at Morningstar.

Khan said Anthropic would need to sustain rapid growth while managing the enormous cost of developing and running its models.

It is the first major developer to go public, so how it trades in the coming days and weeks will be heavily scrutinised to gauge the broader sentiment towards AI following the recent selloff in some parts of the market.

"The key question (for investors) is whether they are comfortable with that range of outcomes and have a sufficiently long-term horizon," Khan said.

OIL DIPS AGAIN

In commodities, oil prices remained under pressure as the growing view that the oil market is turning to a surplus weighed. Brent crude futures were back under $92 a barrel, set for a third weekly fall.

Investors were also focusing on an unprecedented three-way meeting between US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Asia.

The dollar was taking a breather after hitting a 19-month high this week. Hawkish comments from US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller on Wednesday had bolstered expectations of another US rate hike in December.

The euro was at $1.0996, hovering near its lowest since April 2025. The Japanese yen was at 159.48 per dollar and sterling fetched $1.31515.

Waller had said on CNBC that, if the Fed wanted to get inflation down, it needed to take more "aggressive action", either through a half-point increase at the December meeting or by using the post-meeting statement to set market expectations for further hikes at the start of next year.

The comments followed hotter-than-expected inflation data last week, which caused markets to brace for more rate hikes. Traders now price a 90% chance of a 25-basis-point hike next month, the CME FedWatch tool showed.

The 10-year Treasury yield ticked up to 5.08% in European trading, dragging both German bund (DE10YT=RR) and UK gilt yields (GB10YT=RR) up fractionally too.

BERLIN'S BLESSING FOR UNICREDIT

As well as the excitement around Anthropic, Europe's traders also lifted both UniCredit and Commerzbank's shares as Berlin gave its blessing to the takeover of the German bank after years of resistance.

Investor confidence in AI has been shaken over the past few weeks by worries about the profitability of the technology and the massive debt needed to fund and build related infrastructure.

Markets have mostly shrugged off a strong forecast from chipmaker Nvidia this week as uncertainty caused by CEO Jensen Huang's departure last week rattled investors. The company's board dismissed the idea of rehiring Huang.

Armina Rosenberg, portfolio manager and co-founder of Minotaur Capital, said the Anthropic IPO was a useful gauge of investor appetite for AI.

"But one listing won’t settle the debate," she said. "There's a genuine wall of worry right now, and it’ll take a few things to climb it."

data.title: Anthropic Prices IPO At $83 Per Share
data.description:
NEW YORK CITY (dpa-AFX) - Anthropic announced the pricing of its initial public offering or IPO at $83.00 per share, ahead of its planned Nasdaq debut under the ticker symbol 'ANT.'

The offering consists of 980 million shares of Class A common stock, including approximately 956.4 million shares sold by Anthropic and 23.6 million shares sold by certain existing shareholders. Anthropic will not receive proceeds from the sale of shares offered by the stockholders.

The company's shares are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19, 2026, with the offering anticipated to close on November 20, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions.

Major AI Company to Enter Public Markets

Anthropic is best known for developing the Claude family of artificial intelligence models and has emerged as one of the leading companies in generative AI.

The IPO is expected to provide the company with additional capital to support the expansion of its AI technologies across a range of industries, including software, scientific research and healthcare.

Growing Presence in Life Sciences

Beyond its core AI business, Anthropic has increasingly focused on applications in drug discovery and life sciences research. The company has reported research partnerships with six organizations developing new medicines, including Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY), aimed at exploring how Claude can support drug discovery and development.

As pharmaceutical companies seek to shorten drug development timelines and improve research productivity, advanced AI systems are increasingly being explored as tools to support target discovery, molecule design and clinical research.

Offering Details

Anthropic has also granted underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional 147 million shares of Class A common stock.

The IPO is being underwritten by a group of investment banks, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley serving as lead underwriters.

The offering marks one of the most closely watched public listings in the artificial intelligence sector, reflecting growing investor interest in companies developing next-generation AI platforms and their potential applications across industries, including healthcare and life sciences.

data.title: Pharmacy chain Big Caring ends 0.9% higher after $155 million Malaysia IPO
data.description:
By Rozanna Latiff and Yantoultra Ngui

Shares of Big Caring Group (BIGC.KL) closed 0.9% higher in their market debut on Thursday after the Malaysian pharmacy chain raised 637.8 million ringgit ($155 million) in an initial public offering.

  • Big Caring closed at 1.09 ringgit per share, above its IPO price of 1.08 ringgit, after trading between a low of 98 sen and a high of 1.19 ringgit. Malaysia's benchmark KLCI index closed 0.04% lower

  • The company sold 590.5 million new shares while existing shareholders sold 1.29 billion shares at 1.08 ringgit apiece, valuing Big Caring at about 8 billion ringgit

  • Nineteen cornerstone investors, which commit to purchasing shares before trading begins, took up 41.2% of the institutional offering. They included International Finance Corp, JPMorgan Asset Management (Singapore) and Eastspring Investments

  • Big Caring operates 668 pharmacy outlets in Malaysia under brands including BIG Pharmacy, CARiNG Pharmacy, Wellings Pharmacy, Georgetown Pharmacy, Ting Pharmacy and iCare Pharmacy

  • The company plans to use 89.5% of IPO proceeds, or 570.7 million ringgit, to repay bank borrowings and use 30 million ringgit to help fund a new distribution centre

  • Big Caring's net profit for the financial year ended June 30 surged 56.7% to 191.6 million ringgit, while revenue grew 17.9% to 4.02 billion ringgit, underpinned by store launches, higher sales at existing outlets and acquisitions

($1 = 4.1220 ringgit)
